The spots, which resemble a snake, were meant to symbolize the venomous creature, which the talisman could protect against.

Flæs (свин) has many meals, served, and ways prepared in Denmark. One of them is cooking. One common way to cook pork, beef, lamb, and in general, meat in general, is to cook it until it is tender. In order to make sure your meat will be tender, you have to be realistic. If a recipe calls for 2 hours cooking, don't add any "mystery ingredients". If a recipe calls for 15 minutes, the meat is probably cooked:
I followed a recipe for pork slices, and as a test, I cooked 2 identical portions, one in the recipe, and one in my stomach. Danish people, on average eat this at a Danish restaurants.

Life in Denmark is becoming less and less like the United States. The reason is not just that Denmark is very different from the U.S., but also that Denmark has many laws, policies, customs, and traditions that are different from the US. I could write page after page about this, but one thing keeps coming up: How is it that so many American people in the US have no idea what a majority of Americans hold to be important: American values. I have never heard of a single American, and I have met and talked to hundreds of Americans, who hold human rights to be important. I have never heard of a single American who believes in freedom. I have had a Native American tell me that the only American he didn't like was Christopher Columbus. I have had a young black man tell me that he didn't know who George Washington was. I have had people tell me, while looking very serious, that they didn't know if the Holocaust was real. I have even had a few Americans tell me that they were embarrassed to be Americans. These are not rare exceptions, either. These are the usual, norm, and typical Americans. The majority of Americans are against freedom, human rights, and the Holocaust. That is just a fact. The majority of Americans don't know about the important things that are important to being American. The result, as I see it, is that a majority of Americans don't know what they stand for, why they are good, or what is good about them. This is one of the reasons why so many Americans, especially the young and the minorities, are trying to find their identity in something other than America, and I think it is a mistake. A man who does not know his own worth, and a nation which does not know its own worth, is worth very little. I have spent a lot of time in Denmark, and I have noticed that, in Denmark, the majority of people know and respect their country and its history. I live in Sweden, and I have also noticed that the majority of people in Sweden know and respect their country and its history. I have come to the realization that, in the next few decades, Denmark and Sweden are going to be almost as American as the United States. In fact, they are already a part of the American continent. This means that, in the next few decades, the American continent will be filled with people who know and respect their country, and people who don't. In order to keep the whole continent at a high level, I think that America needs to spread American values a lot more. America needs to make sure that the world knows that freedom of speech, human rights, and lack of Nazism, are important American values. If America does not make its values known, America will be seen as a bunch of ignorant people, who don't know what is important in their own country, and who are just war mongers, and their continent will be at a much lower level than it would otherwise be. To put it short: America needs to be known, and America needs to be well-regarded.

Based on the text material, what is the main idea?

The main idea is that America needs to spread its values, and its values are not well-known at the moment. The values are freedom of speech, human rights, and lack of Nazism. As these values are not well-known, America is not held in high regard, and this will lower the level of the American continent.

Could you rewrite the text in a more concise way?

America needs to spread its values, as they are unknown and low-regarded, which will lower the level of the American continent. Its values are freedom of speech, human rights, and lack of Nazism. The ignorant, low-regarded America will lower the level of the continent, unless its values are known.

Apparent to many were the events of Julius Caesar's career when it hit him, as boys and young men, to take the study of oratory (as an instructor, it was not then, it did not, it suited him, take a master to make a master). The controversies, the forums, the public, were filled with muttering and with silence. There was, indeed, in that constant gossip, in that frequent talk, an apparent feeling of Rome among the Roman nobles, which, though in some sense, I may be compelled to say, made them regard the conquest of Egypt as a religious point, as a point of moral duty, with a real and manifest abhorrence of their own fellow Romans, who partook in the war, as one who had declared against Julius Caesar, and, consequently, he who had not: as one, on the contrary, who had joined Antioch in the war against Rome, and as one, more especially, who himself was a secret friend to the Egyptians and Jews.

To a Roman, as often, so from and from such as I have mentioned, in that case, Caesar was conquered.

On Caesar's return from Alexandria, he did as he could, and the common sort, as they heard of Caesar's great victory, believed, of course, that Caesar would in future, having found out by their discourse with one another (for they would of the matter, some of them at least, in the conversations there must be often be heard expressions in favor of the opposite, and, again, the contrary, as, "No wonder, if a man must needs die, the Carthaginians choose to be admitted into the number of the gods, and the gods to die and be revest with immortality) such as Caesar was, extol and commend Caesar, whom they had always hated, whom they had feared, whom they had despised, whom they had reviled, for these very things; for from one or two, as they would often express their discourse, a man of higher rank would come to the Forum, and then the cause was gone, yet that, in the end, the people, for the most part, would be on Caesar's side: "What has this man done and said? why has he made no better defense? why has he offered himself to the Carthaginians?"; but, "he is loved, he is honored, he is immortal, because he is a god, and can make the truth, and the like."

But, on the other hand, "some men, whom are they have not heard, and cannot speak, and will not speak, who are the base and sordaine, the busy and talking, the unlearned and ignorant, who are yea, a great part of them, the companions of the unlearned and wise, the vulgar with the learned and wise, the rabble with their betters: there are liars, there are thieves, there are bastards. There is not, in a truth, any new thing under the sun; but in the same nature, there is much variety; the same things being produced in a different order, or else with a difference of a few parts: as, for instance, in this very case, it hath somewhere been many times told, that there have been men who, for the most part, have had their heads cut off, as it hath been of Caesar, slain by Brutus, by Cassius, by both. So, in this, they say, there is nothing new, for in the sea also the waves are fallen, and in four seasons the leaves are fallen. What is novel there? the falling off of what has grown. If a man plant a field, it grows, and then it falls; or, to give a more familiar instance: if there be a crown of flowers given you, they wither. But the common reports of the events of history are of things ungraceful, and, in some, ridiculous, and, in most, dejecting. As to the flowers, therefore, as they wither, so (say they) the things of mortals decay, and pass away; there is nothing constant in the world. However, it may be, this is the necessary and natural consequence to have a due consideration of the uncertainty of future events, and the vanity of man's works. It is a common saw, and a true one, that every beginning hath a good end; but this is a saw, not without its contrary, and a false one. There is no verse in the poets that is not true, and that has been set to the natural and simple sense; yet many of them are found to be false, without any exception. Now, if you will look for a verse so, in the poets, you shall find this, that every beginning, and the end, hath a bad one. It is as true, that a beginning of a work is often followed with an end, as it is false, that every beginning hath. Now, if it be true that a beginning of a work is often followed with an end, it is not possible that a beginning of a work is always so; for then even the more simple sense is, there is no beginning of all four that I have set down. The sun, it is true, is called a beginning, and an origin, and an archetype, and like it, but for the most part in respect of the honor and admiration which we show by them for the excellence of their effects, not with a true sense; but if they be true, then is a beginning the same as all these, but because they are spoken, not so. Now, if this be so, that a beginning of a work is often followed with an end, what can you be ignorant of? the beginning of a work, as not to know that all our thoughts and discourses are not so framed, that they intend that they shall needs have a cessation, and a contrary end. The work of nature, and the work of hand, are both called event; for it is a true saying, that all things, even to things to be made, are in a manner already, but that their perfection is to come; and the beginning of them is from things past, which things are as if they were. But the things we see, and the issues that attend them, are most part contrary to those intentions. For if a man do the work with care and diligence, it still passeth to the workman; if thou make a bed, it falleth down; if thou make a statue, it turneth its back; if thou make a vessel, it sinketh; if thou make a mirror, it is a lie; if thou make a statue of man, it dieth; if thou gather the issues of nature, they corrupt: all things, in the same nature, work both, but without wrath or malevolence. Therefore, if a man do the work of sewing, his work is to sew together; if he do the work of speaking, his words are spoken; if he do the work of plowing, his work is plowed; if he do the work of a saw, his work is sawn; if he do the work of a beam, his work is a beam; if he do the work of a pillar, his work is a pillar; if he do the work of a wall, his work is a wall; if he do the work of a fortress, his work is a fortress; if he do the work of a watch, his work is a watch; if he do the work of a glass, his work is a glass; if he do the work of a mirror, his work is a mirror; if he do the work of a mill, his work is a mill; if he do the work of a wheel, his work is a wheel; if he do the work of a pin, his work is a pin; if he do the work of a comb, his work is a comb; if he do the work of a cart, his work is a cart; if he do the work of a chair, his work is a chair; if he do the work of a table, his work is a table; if he do the work of a shelf, his work is a shelf; if he do the work of a napkin, his work is a napkin; if he do the work of a towel, his work is a towel; if he do the work of a ceiling, his work is a ceiling; if he do the work of a floor, his work is a floor; if he do the work of a lathe, his work is a lathe; if he do the work of a plane, his work is a plane; if he do the work of a rule, his work is a rule; if he do the work of a compass, his work is a compass; if he do the work of a dial, his work is a dial; if he do the work of a chain, his work is a chain; if he do the work of a saw with a ivory or other steel, his work is a saw; if he do the work of a file, his work is a file; if he do the work of a comb, his work is a comb; if he do the work of a rasp, his work is a rasp; if he do the work of a wrytr, a pen, an inkhorn, a trumpet, a lantern, spectacles, a whistle, a fire, a lyre, a pipe.

But then, you shall not have the same words, nor the same signification, nor reason, nor the semblance of reason, nor a law to follow, nor an example to follow, nor a matter to think of, and a show either of wisdom or foolishness: the words, both to say, and these things to be, are all good and fair; but these, "all is common, and all is not too high, and he that is content, and knows, is best."

But if you consider the things, and their nature, some of them are so, as they are without Alexandria, others as they are without Egypt, without Greece, without the Myis, and the Carians, and the inhabitants of other places, and without, and before, and among, and after, and with, and without, sin, and just.

But this needeth not greatly to be said, for it is manifest, commended by all, and by the wise, necessary; for one of the world, it is enough, and he needeth not to be named: yet for the sake of ornament, Aristotle, if he be a wise man, wrote a book De curis, which is to be as it were, Of the care of the body, and a book Of images, and a preface, or entrance, to his book Peri Poietike, which is to be as it were, the matter of poesy.

But this is not the place to delight in such fancies, or to settle the causes thereof; yet according to the common tradition, it is the nature of all the wise to be content, which was said long ago and everywhere by the poets, and by them:

"Still to rejoice, and to be content, is near to the wise." Men, therefore, that live accordingly to human nature, are content.

But now, that we may see that this is not so, even that which hath been said is, "still to be content," so was it said, "to be content," in like manner as it ought to be: "the poets' place is the highest, and their verse the best, which saith, 'is to be content,'" and in like wise the rest, but only they that be not mad. But the poets in common, with whom this is said, were a great time before, as were all the parts of it, and the perfection of it: for there was a time, when all these things were first invented, framed, and reduced into good order, as they are now, without the possibility of any man rendering them better. So when the Romans had that goodly city of Rome, they framed this verse, "to be content is the best." But the Greeks had not Rome, nor the Romans had not Greece, and therefore they met at Alexandria, and the learned men of Greece, and of Rome, met at Alexandria, to make this verse, and to end all disputation, and to make a memory of their wisdom, which must not be forgotten. And if they were content, why did they not sooner agree? for if now the men of our time were as learned, as they, it might, perhaps, have been done privately. But they were men of great imperfection, and therefore the matter required the multitude, and a great assembly, and the noise of all, and the most part, and learned and unlearned. And when they were assembled, first were made statues of the nine Muses, and of Calliope the chief, a verse or two of hymn to the other gods, and chiefly to Jove, and to the King of the world, and to the other gods. After that, there assembled together five thousand men, or more, of the noblest and the most wise of the Greeks, and of the Romans, and of other countries, as could be chosen, out of all countries, and of all arts and sciences, and of the Senate of Rome, and the Ekklesia of Alexandria, and the Delegation of the Athenians, and the Deputies of the Oracle of Jupiter, and the Bards, and the Poets, and the Philosophers, and the Priests of the gods, that at length they made this verse, which should be a certain rule, and a bridle, and a guide, and a lantern to all wise men of the world, not to Ares, but to content, that is, to be content, and to be at accord.

The poets, and especially the tragic poets, and the inventors of such fables, deserved they not to be cast out of the commonwealth, and to suffer the greatest punishment, and to be condemned as impious, and, if it were possible, to die the death of a female, and to be drowned in a cask in the sea, because they taught, and made verses, and composed them in praise of Alectis, and of Procne, and of Medea, and of other such gods? for they made them to be worshipped. But more grievously have they entangled the sophists and the logicians, who made poetry, and especially the tragic poetry, to be but a kind of show, and a shadow of justice, and of the other virtues.

Let us hear both of them, and first the sophists. As both the sophists, and the logicians, and the poets, and the rhapsodes, and the musicians, and the painters, and the statuaries, and the workers of images, and the makers of all other images of falsehood, and of things that are not, and of shadows, and of similitudes, and of fables, and of lies, and of deceits, and of all other vanities, which the world is full of, seeing they have taken upon them to make a verse of this nature; for it is a verse of all others, and a work of all works, of all sophists, and of all logicians, and of all poets, and of all rhapsodes, and of all musicians, and of all painters, and of all statuaries, and of all workers of images, and of all makers of all other images of falsehood, and of things that are not, and of shadows, and of similitudes, and of fables, and of lies, and of deceits, and of all other vanities, which the world is full of, have said, "all things at the first indeed were not brought in order, but now, the most part, they are set in their places by the greatest Providence, and by their nature, the things which are made by nature, deprived of understanding, and which, for the most part, have not any rule, neither are the same things neither the best, nor the likeliest, but all confused, and thrown about, and the things which are made by art, and by the reason of man, have the rule of all, and of the best, and of the truest things." And whereas Tantalo did afflict the people with hunger, giving them to eat the shadow or similitude of bread, and stones, and whereas Sisyphus did labour, and could never attain, and where Sardanapallus, and Epaminondas, and other such madmen, have done many other things, wherefore the sophists and the logicians, and the poets, and the rhapsodes, and the musicians, and the painters, and the statuaries, and the workers of images, and the makers of all other images of falsehood, and of things that are not, and of shadows, and of similitudes, and of fables, and of lies, and of deceits, and of all other vanities, which the world is full of, have made this verse, that it may be a bridle, and a guide, and an example, and a lantern to all men, that no man should follow after, nor attain to, nor imitate, nor take pleasure in, nor be of this mind, nor be wise, nor to be in the semblance of wisdom, but to be foolish, and to have the minds of beasts, that is, to be content, and to be at accord, and to reverence, and to adore, and to give thanks to the gods, to Jove the highest, to him that giveth, and the King of the world, and to the other gods, to them for all meed, and to ascribe all goodness and felicity, and to be weary of all other things, as if they were not, and to have no hope, nor to think that there shall be any other thing, but that such things as are now, are for ever, and that all the world turneth in a circle, or else in another figure, from the same point, and to the same point, rising again, and setting again, in the same fables, and in the same vanities.

But if this be true, where is the strength, and the wisdom, and the counsel, and the foreknowledge, and the fear of God, which are ascribed to the sophists, and to the logicians, and to the poets, and to the rhapsodes, and to the musicians, and to the painters, and to the statuaries, and to the workers of images, and to the makers of all other images, and to all other men? For they seem to be at the discordance of this verse, and to annul it, and to be ignorant, and to speak without the knowledge, and to make a bruit, and to be in a dream. Gordon Brown: "But if we create all the jobs that can be created in the private sector, we will not in the end, as a country, build the homes, and lay the railways, and build the ships, and maintain the power stations, and provide the infrastructure that a true 21st century economy needs, if we do not create the capacity in the public sector. The great society that I believe in, the open society that I want, is one where a new partnership, between the private sector, the public sector, and the third sector, delivers the great nation that is waiting to come, the and modern society that can be, if we make the right choices, and the right investments, and the right changes this week, and this year."

Alex Salmond: "And we have a plan that we think, we've had the time to develop, to test, to consult, and we think it is the best plan, not just in Britain, but anywhere in the world, for an independent Scotland, a plan that, as I just said, is a very radical plan, even for an independent Scotland, and one that has been, I think, misunderstood in some quarters at home. I've noticed that when the white paper, which sets out our plan in considerable detail, was produced, the headline from the Financial Times, which is, of course, a London-based paper, but which, as I say, has the best economic editors, said: 'More market, faster change: Scotland's Salmond seeks to reassure the Union.' Now, if you don't know, as I said, it was a white paper for an independent Scotland, when it comes to the economy, a very radical plan, and the idea that Scotland, an independent country, would in any sense not be intervening in the market, would be in the market, was completely misquoted. But if you look at the plan, if you look at our white paper, it is a very radical plan, and in many ways, even for an independent country, faster, faster than the changes that we propose, and in many ways, more market, more market than many people at home think that an independent Scotland would need, or require. And I'll just give you some examples. Let me take, first, the issue of energy. 60% of our oil and gas reserves lie beneath the North Sea, and we would use those resources, as an independent country, in the most sustainable way, to power our economy. We would create, as I said, the greenest economy, anywhere in the world. These 2019 predictions are from my series of apocalyptic and dystopian novels Tomorrow Never Dies and The Earth, Our Home, set in my Thrice Upon series with 20+ books. They made their first first appearances in 2003 and 2006, but 2019 is not far from today, so I am sharing this for the first time.

In 2015, I released a collection of six short stories, including one titled “The Last of the Aliens.” It is a science fiction horror, taking place on Earth, around 2020, about a first contact with an alien, leading to the apocalypse. It is a very good story, but when I finished it, I knew that I had more to tell. I needed to tell more. I had more to say, and I knew that I had to write a full-length novel, returning to the series, to tie “The Last of the Aliens” to the rest of the Thrice Upon series. I have started the novel in 2018. I know what the first sentence will be, and the first paragraph, and the first chapter, but I fear that the rest of the novel, I will need to write organically, as I go.

The Last of the Aliens

In the harsh, post-apocalyptic wasteland that Earth has become, the few remaining survivors still remember the stories of the Great Migration, the day when the skies turned red and the aliens came. Vicious, intelligent, and hungry, they descended from the stars to destroy and kill, until the great cities crumbled and fell. Now, in a world that is nothing more than a desolate, lifeless shell, a small band of humans stumbles upon an alien being, one of the last of its kind, who is more complex than they could have ever imagined.

This discovery will not only change the way they see the aliens, but the denizens of Earth as well. Galen, the leader of the small community, wants to protect the alien, but some of the others have painful, memory-filled reasons for hunting it down. In the midst of this, a plague is spreading, and as resources dwindle, a small group, including Galen, his lover, Tania, and the alien, flee to a place that might hold the key to both survival and the fate of the universe itself: the long-abandoned city of Paris.

What they find there will not only challenge their perceptions, but invite them into the mystery of an alien race, and the very fabric of their own. For not only can the alien communicate, but it can share the memories of its species. Memories that span light-years, and millennia. And, for the first time, these new friends share their own: the creation of the human-alien alliance, the Great Migration, and the war that led to the near-extinction of both races. As they share and grieve, the group finds common ground, and love, and, most importantly, hope. But, even as they begin to heal, a dark force stirs, one that, if not stopped in time, will consume the alien and all of the humans he has come to care for.

At 70,000 words, Tomorrow Never Dies is a science fiction and horror novel, and the fourth book in my Thrice Upon series. It is a standalone, but is better read with the others. This novel, like the others, is also a retelling of a fairytale, this time, of “The City of New Gerhaldtown,” based on the short story of the same name, and the stories that inspired it. The novel is a love letter to classic science fiction, and to the fantastic works of Steven Brust, Charles de Lint, and Patricia McKillip.

Excerpt:

Galen had always known that he was different. As a child, he had seen things that others couldn’t, and heard things too, and felt things. He didn’t know if other people were the same, but he did know one thing: he had been born to lead. It was in his very nature to be a protector, a guide, a friend, and a hero, and he would do it all for the sake of the people he loved.

He and Tania had been inseparable since they were children, and as they grew, so did their love. They had been inseparable since the day they first met, and nothing would ever change that. Not even the end of the world.

They had survived, against all odds, and now, they had a future. A new beginning, in a world that was almost like the old one. A world that needed them, and a world that they needed.

A world where they would make their home.

Together.

The end.

Статистическая модель — это математическая модель, которая воплощает в себе набор статистических предположений, касающихся формирования выборочных данных (и аналогичных данных из более крупной совокупности). Статистическая модель представляет, часто в значительно идеализированной форме, процесс генерации данных.

Статистическая модель обычно определяется как математическая связь между одной или несколькими случайными величинами и другими неслучайными величинами. По сути, статистическая модель является «формальным представлением теории» (Герман Адер цитирует Кеннета Боллена).

Все статистические проверки гипотез и все статистические оценки получены с помощью статистических моделей. В более общем плане статистические модели являются частью основы статистических выводов.

However, the keyword "memory leak" is slightly different, as it's more generic. In fact, a "memory leak" is not a problem, as such. Memory leaks are usually just a symptom of some other problem. So, when a user looks for "memory leak", these are the most common scenarios that come to mind:

  - I've heard about a "memory leak", what does it mean? A program can have a memory leak, which usually means, that after some time of the program's running, the amount of free memory is constantly decreasing. However, the term is not about memory in general, but about any resource. For example, file locks, network sockets, drivers, and many more, can have a leak. The term "leak" is the most general form of an unknown resource, which can be lost, or from which we are not able to, or cannot, get back the lost (or "lost", in case of memory, because from the perspective of the program using the memory, we can not distinguish if the memory is free or in use ) units, hence leak. Since memory is the most valuable and often limited resource on a computer, memory leaks are usually more serious than other kinds of leaks, but this is not the only criterion. If a program uses all available memory, it will use more CPU, as a result, the CPU will use more power. In the case of a server, a program with a memory leak will eventually make the system unresponsive, but a client application is more resilient, because it can get the computer restarted, or install more memory. That's why memory leaks in applications are more serious than in system components. So, where other leaks are just the more unimportant, leaks of memory can be critical, and should be avoided. As a result, there are multiple precautions, to prevent memory leaks:

  - In applications, memory should be selected and used as conservative as possible
  - In applications and libraries, free all used resources when they are not needed
  - In applications and libraries, when an object is deleted, free all the memory allocated to it

Рецензия 1: Я не уверен, что это просто тот факт, что Эд Нортон действительно раздражает меня в этом фильме, но я никогда не верил в идею о том, что Бойцовский клуб является своего рода культурным феноменом. Да, это новаторская история, рассказанная с помощью сильного сценария, интересных персонажей и насыщенной кинематографии. Но действительно ли оно достойно такой высокой оценки? Лично я считаю, что он начинает разваливаться на середине, а к концу становится довольно утомительным. Все становится немного детским и надуманным, поскольку история теряет связь со своими базовыми элементами и ярость против машинной атмосферы берет верх. Я испытываю огромное уважение к тому, как был снят этот фильм, но, как и в случае с «Матрицей», я чувствую, что люди придают этому фильму гораздо большее значение, чем он того заслуживает.
Рецензия 2: В фильме рассказывается история мужчин, которые не могут адаптироваться к социальному порядку в современном мире, под руководством Тайлера Дердена, чтобы раскрыть свой природный инстинкт, мужественность и уйти от своей несчастливой жизни.
Обзор 3: Несмотря на хорошую тему, великолепную актерскую игру и важные послания, которые этот фильм передает неортодоксальным способом, я думаю, что он не может связать зрителя с сюжетной линией и оставляет его в мире замешательства. Хотя большинство рецензий находят этот фильм занимательным и интересным, я бы предпочел быть в меньшинстве, которое считает, что этот фильм чрезвычайно переоценен.
Обзор 4: Создание хаоса, взрывов и членство в воинствующей секте - способ избавиться от материальных оков?! Визуальные эффекты завораживают, а история захватывает дух до второй половины. К сожалению, это не заканчивается хорошо.

The film is about a young married couple, Anne (Ruth Olinsky) and Michael (Michael Yurchak) who are both working as doctors in a small, isolated town in Northern Ontario. They are both 30 something (35 in one review, 32 in the other, all 2016, mmm) and, gasp, both are childless. Anne, the chief surgeon, is well-liked by her patients. Michael, her fiancé, is a recently arrived pathologist. Their idyllic relationship turns in unexpected, and ultimately tragic, directions, when Anne is badly beaten by a patient, and, for some reason, doesn't report the attack. She then begins to exhibit strange, almost psychotic behavior, which her family and friends find difficult to understand. Her two closest friends, Doctor Hope (a doctor) and Einar (a journalist), both sense that something is gravely amiss with Anne. One dark, cold, early winter morning, Michael leaves for town on doctor business. He wears his new, snowshoes, but will not need them. Einar, a naive and impressionable young man, is the first person we see. He is standing in the doorway of the local drug store, waiting for the owner to finish counting the cash in his register. When he is finally left alone, Einar grabs the cash register and rushes out, never paying for his 5-cent cigar. This event is not mentioned again. Later, Einar runs into Anne, who is also out, but they don't speak to each other. He meets her fiancé, Dr. Michael, on the road, and they both continue to the next town, where Michael is to give a speech at a hospital. When they say goodbye, Michael promises to return by nightfall. The weather, a cold blue, becomes darker as the men part, and the snow begins to fall. This is the first indication that the weather will be a character all its own. To the snow, we add: second couple: Anne and Michael make a decent ifting, but not exactly a love-match. They are too different and their courtship is confined to a few dates. Love, as they knew it, did not prepare them for each other, and their knowledge of medicine did not prepare them for this. It is a dark and loveless story, but I'm not sure they are intentional. Hope, the journalist, is a drunk, and Einar, his friend, is a doofus. Dr. Price, the local doctor, is a kind man, but his gentle nature is no match for the gathering storm. None of them, not the flawed characters, nor the natural surroundings, can stop what is about to happen.

Michael and Anne, the two main characters, are interested in each other, but not particularly enamored. They go on a few dates, but are not in a hurry to spend their lives together. When Michael asks Anne to marry him, there is no proposal. He simply states the fact that he and Anne would be a good match, and the audience, the Toronto Times (s) can hear the finality of this statement, for this is no marriage proposal. As the film progresses, we see them and we know that there is a strong attraction, but no love, and we see them go on, but not a proposal. We are left to wonder, is there a reason, and if there is, what is it?

In the next scene, Einar, the other main character, is at a store, but he does not buy his cigar. He grabs the cash register and leaves, never paying for it. We see this action as strange, but we do not give it much thought. At the same time, a blizzard of some epic proportions begins to howl around the town. The two other main characters are Anne and Michael, and they are already engaged, but no ring. Michael proposes, but there is no acceptance, because the ring is still on the nightstand. Предложите Java-решение следующей проблемы.

Учитывая целое число n, верните true, если оно является степенью трех. В противном случае верните false.
Целое число n является степенью трёх, если существует целое число x такое, что n == 3^x.

Пример 1:
В: n = 27
Выход: правда
Пояснение: 27 = 3^3

Пример 2:
В: n = 0
Выход: ложь
Пояснение: Не существует x, где 3^x = 0.

Пример 3:
В: n = -1
Выход: ложь
Пояснение: Не существует x, где 3x = (-1).
 
Ограничения:
-231 <= n <= 231 - 1
Продолжение: можете ли вы решить эту проблему без циклов/рекурсии?

Кратко изложите полученную статью.

Математика и искусство связаны по-разному. Математику называют искусством, движимым красотой. Математику можно обнаружить в таких видах искусства, как музыка, танец, живопись, архитектура, скульптура и текстиль. Однако эта статья посвящена математике в изобразительном искусстве.
Математика и искусство имеют давнюю историческую связь. Художники использовали математику с IV века до нашей эры, когда греческий скульптор Поликлет написал свой Канон, предписывая пропорции, предположительно основанные на соотношении 1:√2 для идеального обнаженного мужчины. Настойчивые популярные утверждения об использовании золотого сечения в древнем искусстве и архитектуре без надежных доказательств. В эпоху итальянского Возрождения Лука Пачоли написал влиятельный трактат «О божественной пропорции» (1509 г.), иллюстрированный гравюрами на дереве Леонардо да Винчи, об использовании золотого сечения в искусстве. Другой итальянский художник, Пьеро делла Франческа, развил идеи Евклида о перспективе в таких трактатах, как «De Prospectiva Pingendi», и в своих картинах. Гравер Альбрехт Дюрер много раз ссылался на математику в своей работе «Меленхолия I». В наше время художник-график М.К. Эшер интенсивно использовал мозаику и гиперболическую геометрию с помощью математика Х.С.М. Коксетера, а движение Де Стейля под руководством Тео ван Дусбург и Пит Мондриан открыто придерживались геометрических форм. Математика вдохновила такие текстильные искусства, как лоскутное шитье, вязание, вышивка крестиком, вязание крючком, вышивка, ткачество, изготовление турецких и других ковров, а также килим. В исламском искусстве симметрия проявляется в таких разнообразных формах, как персидский гирих и марокканская плитка зеллиге, каменные ширмы с отверстиями в могольских джали и широко распространенные своды мукарнас.

Исследование, опубликованное ранее в этом году Зи и ее командой, изучало роль света во сне для здоровых взрослых в возрасте от 20 лет. Сон всего одну ночь при тусклом свете, например, у телевизора с выключенным звуком, повышал уровень сахара в крови и частоту сердечных сокращений у молодых людей во время эксперимента в лаборатории сна. Предыдущие исследования показали, что повышенная частота сердечных сокращений в ночное время является фактором риска будущих сердечных заболеваний и ранней смерти, а более высокий уровень сахара в крови является признаком резистентности к инсулину, что в конечном итоге может привести к диабету 2 типа.

1. Reversible Computing. Reversible computing is a model of computing, which could be very powerful, but apparently not practical (at least not in a certain, very usual, sense). The problem is, that in order to achieve reversibility, some additional information is needed, which is called reversibility certificate. The problem is then, not to solve the model, but to find an efficient solution. In the case of reversible computation, the problem is, to find a computation that is already given, and to compute the certificates. It turns out, this could be very powerful, but the price to pay is that the whole model is not practical. All known solutions use an additional resource: the so-called inverse. In fact, this is not really a "resource", but a penalty, so to say. The main task is to compute a function, the other task to compute its inverse. The latter is a penalty, because it is much worse than the former. The inverse has the extra complexity, which is the same as the computation, but the exponent is logarithmic. While for the main task we need a time linear to the input size, for the inverse, we need a time exponential to the size multiplied by the logarithm. This is a general fact, and it is true for all known solutions, but there is no general proof for this. This is a well-known fact, but the original proofs are of no interest for us, because they rely on the model. We have several models, and all these statements are true for all of them. These are, the quantum circuit model, the one-way circuit model, the model of circuits with delayed input, the quantum program, the exchange model, and all others. These are just some names, and there is some overlap. The reason is, that all of them are based on quantum mechanics, and work with quantum operations, circuits and programs, but the input and the output (if there is one) of a quantum operation, program or a circuit is not a part of the model, but are mathematical objects, which are manipulated. So, the formal side, which is a necessary side, does not say anything about practicality. For a quantum book, this is the theoretical part, and it takes only a very, very small part of the whole book. To get a better understanding of the whole subject, one have to look beyond, into the practical side. For the practical side, the original models are not sufficient. In the practical side, the models (except from the one-way model) suggest that the target (if it exists) of a quantum operation, is an input of an inverse. One of the most natural, and by far the most popular, is to add an inverse to the model, and ask for a reversiblity certificate. This is reasonable, and in the case of circuits, it is called Toffoli's gate.

As I mentioned, the practical side is not covered by the models. For example, to have a reversible computation in mind, one has to have a set of gates, a set of data, and maybe more, but not just the reversibility certificate. The certificate, in general, states, that a computation, a set of input, and a set of gates, is reversible, and this is a good start, but it does not say, that this is efficient. To have an efficient reversibility certificate, the following points are necessary:

1. To have a polynomially large input.
2. To have a gate, which is reversing.
3. The number of gates should be polynomially large.
4. The certificate should be polynomially larger than the input.

While 1., 2. And 3. Are well-known, the last condition, 4, is not that well known. It states, that the reversibility certificate, should not be too large, as the size of the certificate, in general, is the size of the input, plus the size of the computation, but multiplied by the logarithm of the input size. To avoid too much, the ideal situation (a linear reversibility certificate) is, that the input size is 1, and this is the simplest case, which is, in general, solvable.

Создайте краткое и лаконичное изложение статьи на основе ее аннотации.

Обучение за несколько шагов (FSL) — один из ключевых будущих шагов в машинном обучении, привлекающий большое внимание. В этой статье мы фокусируемся на проблеме понимания диалога FSL, которая содержит две тесно связанные задачи: обнаружение намерений и заполнение слотов. Доказано, что понимание диалога приносит большую пользу от совместного изучения двух подзадач. Однако такое совместное обучение становится затруднительным в сценариях с несколькими выстрелами: с одной стороны, разреженность выборок значительно усложняет моделирование связи между двумя задачами; с другой стороны, еще меньше изучено, как совместно изучать несколько задач в режиме «несколько шагов». В ответ на это мы представляем FewJoint, первый эталон FSL для совместного понимания диалога. FewJoint предоставляет новый корпус с 59 различными диалоговыми доменами из реальных промышленных API и платформу кода для упрощения постановки эксперимента FSL, что, как ожидается, будет способствовать развитию исследований в этой области. Кроме того, мы обнаружили, что недостаточное выполнение настройки «несколько кадров» часто приводит к шумному распределению между двумя подзадачами и нарушает совместное обучение. Чтобы решить эту проблему, мы направляем слот с явной информацией о намерениях и предлагаем новый механизм шлюзования доверия, который блокирует информацию о намерениях с низкой степенью достоверности для обеспечения высококачественного обмена. Кроме того, мы представляем стратегию метаобучения на основе Reptile для достижения лучшего обобщения в невидимых областях с несколькими выстрелами. В экспериментах предложенный метод обеспечивает значительные улучшения в двух наборах данных и обеспечивает новые современные характеристики.

Georg Frobenius: In 1887, Frobenius was one of 18 mathematicians who founded the journal Mathematische Annalen, which he edited until 1918. He published a series of 10 papers there on the theory of modular functions, which was his specialty. The journal, now owned by Springer, is still being published, and its 188th volume was just released, containing 63 pages on various topics of modern mathematics. The 64 pages before that one, however, are an even more special one, since they contain the solution for a problem posed by Frobenius in 1899. The papers deal with the study of «effective’ conditions for the vanishing of Riemann’s modular function” and they are direct successors of the work of Frobenius.
You can download the entire paper, but I made this book, so I prefer my own one, and this one is in the Latin language, for the same reason.

Padé and Frobenius studied the same function, but independently, and neither acknowledged the other’s work. But, in the 26 years between 1899 and 1925, their work became well known, to the extent that, for example, the function is sometimes referred to as the Frobenius-Padé function, or as the Padé-Frobenius function. This shows that the work of two mathematicians who worked on the same problem at the same time, and who never cited each other, can be as important as it could be, and yet deserve recognition on their own. So, here, the fact is more than 120 years, and I don’t need to have a PhD to appreciate the work of both authors, and to understand that the title of the work presented by each of them is a fundamental contribution. If you eat (or start eating) also food and food products recommended by the new US administration, you should try a new slogan – eat for the military, for law and order, for building walls, for large infrastructure, for your own health.

1. Eat less, you won't die, you'll feel even better. Don't think that I mean calorie-restricted diet. My point is that our standard American way of eating is about how much, not how good food is. If you eat less of what you normally eat, you won't need the same variety, and you can eat less. The idea of eating right, meaning a more healthy diet, is often connected with a lot of new foods, new habits, and so on. I'm not saying that any of these things are unimportant, but I am saying that you don't have to do them all. Start with something you're already used to – eat less food, and you'll find that you don't need all the new foods, and all the new habits, and so on.

2. Eat a plant-based diet. This is a common recommendation, and for good reasons. If you want to eat a more healthy diet, and you also want to eat less meat, the first thing you should do is to add more plants. This is a good idea, but if you're like I was a few years ago, you might be thinking: I don't know how to do that. You see, we live in a society where meat is the main dish. But back in our evolutionary past, the situation was quite the opposite: plants were the main food, and meat, if it happened, was a precious but minor part of the meal. I think we could learn a lot from our ancestors, and that we should bring plants back to the center of the plate. Try it, and you might find you don't need all the new foods, and all the new habits, and so on.

3. Eat a low meat diet. The (presumptive) title of this section is a purpose, not a result. As for the means, if you want to eat a low meat diet, I have a suggestion: eat fewer meats. This is, perhaps, too basic to mention, but I think it's worth saying. We've been taught about all the new, healthy foods, and all the new, healthy habits, and so on, but not how to start eating them. I'm not saying that these things are unimportant, but I am saying that you don't have to do them all. Start with something you're already used to – eat less meat, and you'll find that you don't need all the new foods, and all the new habits, and so on.

4. Eat less means, more plants. I know what you're thinking: easier said than done. I get it. The problem, though, is that the onus is on you to change. I'd like to suggest that we reframe the issue, and think about what the food industry needs to do, instead of what we need to do. Here, in no particular order, are some suggestions, and maybe a few requests:

4.1. Don't offer a meat-based meal, unless there's also a plant-based side dish. This means restaurants, cafeterias, and everyone else who serves food for the public, or for the people you work with.

4.2. Don't be afraid to make a big batch of something. Cook, then eat, then freeze, then eat, then eat, then eat, and then eat again. Don't be afraid to eat the same food more than once in a week. The food industry: make more foods for 1, 4, or 10, that keep well, and reheat well.

4.3. This is not a food-preparation show, but I'm going to make a food-preparation recommendation. Cook more plants. It doesn't take all day, and you don't need a degree in the field. In fact, you can cook a couple of meals in under an hour. The food industry: offer take-out salads and soups, and label which ones are meat-based, and which ones are not.

4.4. Don't be a dieter. Just eat less meat. Set a personal, non-dieting rule: once a week, make a plant-based meal, and eat it for dinner. The rule will be enough. You don't have to count calories, and you don't have to pick at a salad in the corner. Eat a healthy, plant-based dinner in the same mix with your other, favorite, non-plant-based meals. Your food: try not to make a big deal about the fact that you're eating less meat. Just do it.

4.5. Don't snack. Well, you can, but I'm going to challenge myself to snack more on plants, and leave the other option for when I'm eating a meal. The food industry: I don't care if you sell snacks, but I would like to be able to walk into your store, and find a place for my mouth that doesn't involve meat, if I need a mouthful of food. I'd like to be able to eat at your place, whether you're selling a meal, or a bag of snacks, and have a few plant-based options available.

4.6. Don't have a reason to eat more meat. Just eat less of it. Set a personal, non-diet, non-principle, non-new-information rule: when you show up for a meal, and there's more meat than you want, ask for a side of whatever plants the meal has, or ask for a plant-based alternative. Don't think about it, just do it. It's a rule, and you don't have to think about the rule. The food industry: offer a couple of meals that don't have meat, and don't make a big deal about the fact that one of the meals doesn't have meat.

4.7. Don't think about it. Just eat less meat. I know I've given you a lot of suggestions, but the bottom line is this: you don't need a reason to eat less meat. It can be a free response to an impending meal. Just do it. Your food: this is, perhaps, too basic to mention, but I think it's worth saying. Don't make a big deal about the fact that you're not eating as much meat. Just do it. Don't make a separate course out of salads, which I fear to be the case in the picture above, taken at a restaurant I visited.

If you want to go further, that's your business. But you don't have to. I'm not saying these are the things you can do to eat a more healthy diet, I'm saying these are the first, easy things you can do, and that you don't need all the new foods, and all the new habits, and so on. Start your kids, and the food industry, and I think we'll start seeing better results.

Based on the text, what are some practical steps to eat a more plant-based diet, according to the author?

- Eat a low meat diet, which can be achieved by eating less meat.
- Make a plant-based meal at least once a week, and eat it for dinner.
- When offered a meal with more meat than desired, ask for a side of plants or a plant-based alternative.
- When snacking, choose plants over other options.
- When cooking, cook more plants and offer plant-based take-out options (salads, soups, etc.).
- When serving food, make sure a plant-based side dish accompanies a meat-based main dish.
- When eating out, ask for plant-based options and choose establishments that offer plant-based meals and snacks without making a big deal about the lack of meat

Homologous recombination (HR) is the principal mechanism of CRISPR-Cas-independent editing in eukaryotic cells. This post presents 25 ways to improve your academic writing.

Writing a paper is a tough task, which requires a lot of hard work and effort. An essay writing may not be a piece of cake only when you have thousands of essays of this kind already. You may feel frustrated, especially as you know that your teacher has to review several masterpieces and, thus, your work will be compared to the works your classmates have done. Here are 10 tips that will help you write better texts and improve your essay writing skills.

1. Plan: Start with planning. Think about the subject and how you can interpret it. You should make a plan of your paper and arrange it into logical parts.

2. State the purpose: State the purpose of your writing. Tell your teacher what your objectives are and how you are going to reach them.

3. Be concise: You don’t need to write a lengthy paper. A well-structured 5-7-paragraph essay is enough.

4. Know the topic: Before you start writing, make sure you know what the topic is. If the topic is too broad, you should narrow it down. Ask yourself what the topic is about and why the paper is important.

5. Know the audience: Your teacher is your audience. Imagine what they want to see in your paper.

6. Grab the reader’s attention: The first sentence is the most important. You should start with a hook to grab the reader’s attention.

7. Use clear language: Avoid using idioms and colloquial language. Write with simple and clear language that everyone can understand.

8. Use strong assertions: Do not be afraid to make strong statements. Make sure that these statements are true and you can support them with evidence.

9. Use evidence: Evidence is your support. Use facts, examples, and quotes to prove your point.

10. Use counterarguments: You cannot ignore opposing views. Look up and analyze opposing arguments and states. Show that you acknowledge them, but also make it clear why they are not reliable.

11. Be correct: Check for grammar and spelling mistakes. You can use online tools to do it.

12. Write and rewrite: Do not write the first lines first and the last lines last. Write a draft and then edit and rewrite it.

13. Use an outline: Before you start writing, create an outline of your paper. Make a plan and then follow it.

14. Use the right format: Make sure the format of your paper is the format required. Check the requirements if you have any.

15. Use headings: You may use headings to differentiate text. This can help the reader focus and understand your paper better.

16. Avoid plagiarism: Do not copy other works. Check your paper for plagiarism.

17. Make it original: Your writing should be original. Do not copy other works.

18. Read: If you want to improve your writing skills, you should read more.

19. Use concise sentences: Do not use wordy sentences. Say your message shortly and clearly.

20. Pay attention to the structure: Pay attention to the structure and format of your paper. Your essay should have a logical and clear structure.

21. Be creative: Your writing should reflect your personality. Show your creativity.

22. Pay attention to the title: The title is a part of your paper, so pay attention to it. Make sure the title is appropriate and reflects the content of your paper.

23. Use a sample: You can get help from a sample. Compare and adopt the strong parts, but do not plagiarize.

24. Stay focused: Stay focused. Do not go off-topic.

25. Take a break: Take a break after finishing your paper. This will help you see the weaknesses and strengths of your work better. You will be able to read it with different eyes and understand what can be improved.

Based on the text, how can you summarize the tips for improving academic writing?

1. Know the purpose, audience, and topic
2. Use a hook in the first sentence
3. Write with clear language
4. Use evidence and counterarguments
5. Check for grammar and spelling
6. Use an outline and format
7. Be creative
8. Take a break after writing

Write a 5-7-paragraph essay about a specific topic, adding a hook in the first sentence, using clear language, evidence, and counterarguments, and being free from grammatical errors. Use an outline and format, and take a break before proofreading. Consider the purpose and audience, and stay focused.

When I was in secondary school, I also spent a few years giving basic high school science to the younger students. When I saw my former students, the ones who have been 16 when I'd taught them, later, doing quantum physics, I asked them if they knew where they had studied. I was, or rather, I still am, surprised by the number of people who, in my time, were convinced of the existence of a "quantum physics class" in high school. After all, the atom, the energetics, the radiation, it's all quantum physics, but in the year I started studying physics, 2011, I still can ask most people why they want to study physics, why not, and I can even wonder if I speak to one of the few people, who is (at that age) interested in a career without a clear goal. But the main reason I didn't get an answer I had a very clear one: "I like numbers and the way they work." I didn't get an answer, but those who, at that time, gave me an opening for a conversation, usually also didn't say "numbers" and an idealistic share, but they also used words on what they will be (or would like to be) in 5, 10, 20, 30... Years, and I can tell you that, 25 years before, in 1880, a student of mine told me that he would like to be a teacher, and 50 years afterwards, in 2030, to become a computer specialist. Given the fact that he already had a good part of the latter specialty, I suggested him to use a computer, but as he didn't know much about it, I asked him what a computer is. He said: "It's this big thing in the computer room at school." I used the opportunity to convince him that it was better to use the word calculator, and that I will buy him one, which I did, a Texas Instruments 88C. But I digress. What a student is saying, is, that knowledge and learning is a steady stock, it has something to do with something intangible, but stable. We all know that what we learned in school is stable, and that the formal, static knowledge is a part of knowledge, and the knowledge we got is unburdened by the fact that it is of the past. But my student, who wanted to become a computer specialist, and in addition to this, already had a good track record of gathering knowledge, showed me with the examples I didn't understand all, but the general view was: knowledge is about dealing with the truth, the more knowledge we have, the more truth we know, and therefore, knowledge and truth are the same, or, at least, knowledge is a part of truth. I, as a physics student, also learned that the more knowledge we have, the more we understand, and the more we understand, the more we know, and the more we know, the more we understand. This is a valid insight, but in the world of science, it is not a law, but a statement, because it is not true in general. The more knowledge we had in the 19th century, the better we understood some things, but there are also many things, which, when we try to understand them with the available knowledge, we cannot understand. It shows very clearly in the 19th century, when A, the available knowledge, and U, the problems we were not able to understand yet, were in a state of permanent change, and around 1900, A had advanced so much, that a lot of problems, that were only known to be difficult, became understood. This was the so-called Poincaré-Rashevsky effect of self-organization of knowledge. To visualize the knowledge, we will use a line. The line is for the knowledge, and the length of the line is a measure for the amount of knowledge we have. In the beginning of the 19th century, the knowledge line was short, and the further we are in the future, the longer the knowledge line. So, the length of the knowledge line is a measure for the amount of knowledge we can have, using it, and the longer the line, the more we know. This is a valid insight, but it is only a statistical insight, and therefore, in the long run, it gives a very rough indication for the amount of knowledge we have. So, we need a more precise method. The precise method is to use the one-dimensional knowledge line, and divide it into many segments, each segment with a certain size. The size of the first segment is very small, the size of the second segment is somewhat larger, the size of the third segment is even larger, and it holds for all segments, that they get larger as we move further from the beginning of the knowledge line. This means, that the length of the segments is a measure for the number of this segment. The knowledge segments are usually divided by a branch, they are called size and number of the segment. The names for the sizes are: 1st segment, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, ... For the units, the size of the segment is: for the 1st segment, unit, for the 2nd segment, sub-unit, for the 3rd segment, sub-sub-unit, ... It is possible to convert the units to the size, but for the sizes, this is not necessary, as they are used in the conversion only. So, for the sizes, we use the conversion factor 1. Of the 19th century, they used it for the length, and the volume, and the weight, and all other physical quantities. The conversion factor, which should express, that it is a conversion, was 1:1, and so, for the knowledge, the conversion was: the same, in this form, or in words: identic. Now, we can write a table, that shows the knowledge, which belongs to a time period, and the conversion, that connects the knowledge of this period with the previous and the next period.

A tank, a truck, or a bicycle is not the subject, but I noticed that some people in the US have shown a big and increasing interest on their versions of the "green" and "melting" events in recent years.

What can be the reason? I suppose that this is primarily a matter of the big business and the policies of the US, the governments, the influence of the environmental lobbies, and so on, but perhaps this is also the last attempt of the US (at some level, the fact that some Americans actually come to the conclusions that their presence in the North America is a benefit, a chance for their survival, a hope for the environment, a thing, in some cases, even ecological, environmental, eco, and so on. What the people of the US, who are not able to witness the Russia invasion and occupation of the former Soviet republics (Cuba, Yugoslavia, Vietnam, Laos, and East Germany) of the last 50 years, see geology and geologists, but in Russian

As the ruling family of Russia (which is democratic in some sense, at least for formal reasons) is not exactly open about their thoughts and policies, it is difficult to know what exactly Russian president Vladimir Putin thinks in regard to global warming, and whether this is an issue for the world. But we can try to understand what he is saying, at least, taking into account.

Vladimir Putin, the leader of the Russian Federation, holds a number of high offices and even more urgent responsibilities. One of them, which I mention from time to time, is to defend the interests of the Russian people and the Russian state on the global scene, including the global scene of science. When Putin speaks about climate, he is sure to mention – just once, but quite often – that the Earth's climate changes. In these very cases, he is not even a pioneer, because this is a fact. When he speaks, however, about the reasons of climate change, he never mentions the fact that over the last century many countries, including Russia, reduced their emissions, or that in the recent 25 years, after the fall of the USSR, the emissions in Russia were reduced by 30-40%. All this is just famous. When he speaks about the ways to fight climate change, he frequently speaks about the need to switch to so-called "green energy". The Russian authorities have been doing this for many years, but so far they have not succeeded in this, despite generous state support and numerous state programs. The reason for this is quite simple – the more the state invests in "green energy", the more the population suffers from the resulting high taxes and the falling living standards. That is why, when the Russian people came to understand that the state is not going to abandon its massive programs in traditional and already optimized for emissions energy, they began to reevaluate their entire energy and industry policies. This is what we can see in the last 5 years or so, when there has been more and more talk of "deindustrialization" and a "downscaled economy" in Russia. But in spite of the fact that the situation where the state is investing into "green energy" and, at the same time, the population is suffering from the consequences of this, looks like a deadlock, one should not think that this is indeed a deadlock. What we have is a certain, for now, dead-end line in the development of the Russian economy – a line that the state wants to move the Russian economy to, but it is not able to find a way to make the population accept this. And the situation is quite paradoxical, and the reasons for this are quite obvious. The Russian state, in the capacity of an absolute one, has taken this course, but, strangely enough, the population has its own preferences and, while the state is investing in "green energy", it continues to prefer the existing industry, wanting it to continue developing. This is not a contradiction between the state and the people, because usually the relations between the state and people are not a contradiction, but a confrontation. But the state and the people in this case are not on opposite sides, they are, so to speak, on equal footing. This is a kind of parallel, but still not a contradiction, because the preference of the people, in the final count, is not a developed, but a limited and simple society. The Russian society, as a simple, not very developed, and simple-minded one, would like to have modern, but at the same time highly developed coal, oil, and gas industries, and, at the same time, is not interested in the development of "green energy" (like solar and wind, which have not reached the point of maturity, and hydroelectric power, which, in case it is possible at all, is very expensive). In this case, the people want the government to invest in traditional energy, but not too much, so that the economy would not suffer, the taxes would not be too high, and the living standards would not drop. In other words, the people want a progressive economy, but at the same time, they want to keep the energy of the industrial revolution they have already acquired, and, at the same time, a stable, or even, to improve living standards. In Russia, the state, which claims to be a responsible one, and the Russian people, which, as we see, has some rather reactionary views, contradict each other. On the one hand, the state wants to help the population, and, on the other, to modernize the country's economy, including the energy sector. This contradiction is impossible, and, as a result, the state is unable to find a way out. The situation is, as I said, paradoxical, but the conclusion is obvious – the state, as a positive force, and the people, as a negative one, are incompatible. When the state is in the process of making a historic break in its history, and people, of preventing that break, things clash, and, in this case, the end of the dead-end line in the development of the Russian economy is over – a dead-end line where the state is trying to get, but the people do not let it.

This is, naturally, not the first time the Russian leadership is speaking of the need to fight "excess" and "harmful" emissions, of the need to transfer to "green energy". It has been so speaking since the 1970s. Back then, in the Soviet years, the theme was called "glocal" challenges, and it included, among others, the ecological damage and aftermath of the Third World, and, especially, the intensified arms race with the United States, that was, at that time, the USSR's main strategic partner. Even back then, Russia recognized the need to help those Third World countries, which suffered, among other reasons, from the "negative" consequences of the arms race. This, however, is not the arms race, but a consequence of the industrial activities, and, in this case, Russia is not to blame. By the late 1980s, the problem of "glocal challenges" came to the forefront, and the Soviet leadership realized that it could not remain indifferent to the fates of people in other countries, and, thus, announced the "Scientific and Technical Program on the Conversion of the Military-Industrial Complex", which, among other things, provided for the transfer of the arms industry to "green" (i. E. Ecological) types of production, and, more importantly, for the provision of extensive financial and, if necessary, military and political aid to the countries of the Third World. This program, however, was never put into practice, and, on the contrary, the arms industry in Russia was growing and expanding.

In the 1990s, Russia inherited the legacy of the defunct Soviet Union, including the problem of "glocal challenges", or, more precisely, the consequences of the arms race with the United States, one of the sources of which were the countries of the Third World. The Russian leadership, guided by the ideas of liberalism and conscience, announced its willingness to cooperate with these countries, and even presented them with the "Brasstacks" plan, a kind of a set of proposals, according to which all the weapons in the countries of the Third World had to be withdrawn, and the conflicting sides had to sit down at a negotiation table and discuss the most problematic aspects of their relations, including the arms race, with the benefit of Russian mediation. He also came back for the Salon of 1888, where he showed another three paintings. In 1887, two years after Gauguin's return to the Salon, Van Gogh exhibited at the Salon des Refusés, a parallel exhibition for the yearly Salon, with works that were rejected by the Salon's jury. He showed four paintings, including The Potato Eaters and five drawings, including Woman Rolling a Cigarette [of a earlier exhibition]. I don't always use the time and effort to write a full post, especially when I don't know what someone is talking about. So, let me do this in a post: I recently read about the drink called "Mead" and the fact that it has bacteria interested me. I also looked for ways to make it, and I remember the following video, but I didn't treat the topic with much respect, because I was more focused on the fact that this person is not paying attention to the large amounts of honey, than in the fact that he's drinking in a glass. This video involved a lot of reading, too, because it tackled a difficult topic, and the author was pretty well informed. I learned a lot of things from it, but not directly, so I had to look at it indirectly through a few reflections.

1. Looking for honey in a jar, I was amused by this comic, and the first thing I thought is, that the guy looks a bit like a bear. This is a bear, and not an actor, was known in the 19th century. But I digress, let's see other things.

2. This mead, as it is called, involves a lot of topics. As a self-motivated learner, I wanted to learn more about mead, and as the video that I found most interesting was about the history of mead, I wanted to learn when it was made first. So I looked, and the information that I found was that mead was first made some 10,000 years ago. I don't think it was made the same way, but the claim was good enough for me to take it as a starting point.

3. 10,000 years is a long time, and for the first time, while reading about how mead is made, I got a good, non-scientific, non-mathematical idea: if a person, our very own ancestors, knew that the honey mead was a great, and that the honey would keep for a long time, they probably also knew that over time, honey mead would evolve, and take many forms. And I won't be surprised that they would come to the conclusion that honey mead is a most welcome, perhaps even a necessary, intoxicant. So, if a 19th century beekeeper told me that he had a problem with the bees, and that the bees were acting strange, and that he was pretty sure that there was something wrong with the bee, and that he tried everything, except for calling the village witch, I would say: this bee has a problem with the weather, and probably with the plants, but he doesn't care as long as he can enjoy the berries. But if he added that the bees were drinking only the berries, he would surely imply that berry-wine is nectar's preferred daughter, which would in my country would surprise me, as bee-man mentioned, as wine-making (from grapes) comes from France, and not from our ancestors. But I am talking about bee-fruit: honey, so if I were able to translate his words to a language I know, I would say: mead.

There is a common misconception in the first video, and that is that honey wine (mead) is made from a wine-flower. Mead is usually made from a beer-flower, and in our region, the beer-flower is the hops. In a 19th century, with the abundance of flowers, it is quite odd that this is the one that was used, but there it is. So, if a bee-keeper, a medieval-bee-keeper, told us about his beer, he would call it mead. Now, mead is a strong, and a sweet, drink, and for that reason, it is rarely made (if not in special occasions, like to celebrate the end of a good season). So, our ancestor may have called it a good season, and, since he was a king, he ordered his messengers to bring a message to the people: For I declare, people, that this year's beer, is good! (well, he may not use a written text, but the villagers would understand him, and the word would be spread.) In a similar way, the ancestors in our area knew when to declare a good year for wine. Now, they didn't make neither in beer, nor in wine, but that is because they lived so far from the Mediterranean Sea, and the climate was not suitable. As for the honey, well, that was a given, and they probably made some, as the climate was suitable for bees, but it was not the most important. So, the king declared: This year is good, and the beer is good!

Only a few centuries, and we, in the first country of the Empire, had the pleasure to enjoy both, wine and beer, neither of them being good. We found ourselves in a terrible kingdom: the north, a place were they had no culture, no civilization, and no wine (according to the way they made it). We didn't want to adopt their barbarian ways, but sometimes, we had to. And I know one thing: as they adopted our clothes, and our mill, I am quite sure, that they didn't make beer, but mead. Our words, for the liquor made from the nectar, were wine, and no, the king didn't declare: This year, I declare, the beer is good! Because the word, good, was reserved for the Empire, for civilization, and for wine. So, the king declared: This year, I, the king, declare, this year, the wine is good!

Back to the time when we, in the 19th century, studied the history of mead, and were told, mead was the beer of the Aryans, we were taught that the Aryans, a civilization far beyond the others, had a great wisdom, and made a most intelligent decision, when they started making beer, instead of wine. Well, the wisdom of the Aryans does not need proof, but one can't be too careful. Let's ask a 19th century, when was the Aryans, and did they have this beer, or wine? And when we learn, that the oldest Aryan written sources tell of wine, we are a bit puzzled, as the available Aryan sources, the Rig-Veda, describes wine in superlatives, as the greatest of all drinks. So, if the Aryans had wine, why did they make a different drink, mead, and call in beer? One reason for this, the discovery of beer, but not a sufficient one, as the Aryans, like many other nations, like the Assyrians, the Babylonians, and the Egyptians, had wine for at least 2000 years before the birth of mead. It was only after that, around 1200, that mead became known, and even then, it was just in some places, while the north, like Scotland, was still far from mead. So, at a time, the British had wine, and they didn't call it beer, but mead, and later, beer. How is this possible, that mead, which was so highly regarded, became so unpopular, that it was replaced by beer? The answer is, that beer is a product of a high civilization, while mead is a primitive, barbarian drink. And when the British became civilized, they abandoned mead, and adopted beer, just like the Egyptians did, just like the Assyrians did, just like the Babylonians did, just like the Greeks did, just like the Romans did, just like the Amerindians did, when they became civilized.

The story, so far: mead, essential, highly regarded, the best of all drinks, the drink of the gods, the drink of the Aryans. Mead, so highly regarded, that the Aryans, who had wine, decided to invent a new drink, mead, and called it beer. But as wine became scarce, mead, or beer, became less prestigious, and when wine disappeared, around 3000 BC, mead, or beer, became less prestigious, and people tried to imitate wine with mead, but as they failed, mead, or beer, became even less prestigious, and people tried to forget that they needed wine, and invented the story of its disappearance, and the great loss, the Aryans, sustained, and how they overcame it. But one can't deny, that a loss, a great loss, it was, the disappearance of wine, and the loss of mead, or beer, with it. Write a horror story, set in the 80s, in third person, about five people, including one child, trapped in a malfunctioning, escalator, focusing on the sensory, and the psychological impairments the protagonists experience. The story should be written in past tense, and make use of present tense flashbacks to show the characters' backstories. The protagonist's flashbacks should not be directly connected to their current predicament, but rather, they should reveal important character details. The story should contain at least one plot twist, and be 2,500 to 3,000 words long. The story should also contain at least one graphic and vivid description of trauma, and should be written in a literary, and unsettling style.

On the surface, the escalator is like any other in the city. It hums a smooth, familiar melody as it carries its load of human cattle. But today, it carries more than just the five who stepped onto its gleaming steps. It carries their lives, their history, and a darkness that, for once, is not of their making.

It is a perfect day, all things considered. The sun is shining, a light breeze is in the air, and the few white, puffy clouds in the sky look soft enough to dab one's face with. The kind of day that, in spring, makes one forget the chill of winter that, until then, had a death grip on the city. The kind of day that makes one forget the war, at least for a little while.

Janet, a nurse, is the first to step onto the escalator. She's heading to her sister's wedding, a ceremony that, considering how long it's been in the making, is as much for the family that as it is for the bride and groom. Janet's not a people person, but she's attached to her family. She loves them, and they love her despite her faults. So, here she is, on her way to a wedding, her blue eyes and long, tan face set in an easy smile.

As she steps on the escalator, a memory floats up, a present-tense memory. She's tried to push it away, but it's no use. It's there, right in front of her, the day the war found her.

The second to arrive is David, a soldier. At first, he doesn't see Janet. When he does, he hesitates, but only for a moment. She was a stranger to him, a civilian, and a woman, and he's seen how easily they can be killed. So, he pushes past her, not too closely, but not too far away either. He's on his way to a court martial, for following his instincts, for not following orders, and for failing his superiors. He's on his way to being stripped of his rank, with no way to appeal the decision. A decision that's been made, and is irrevocable.

David's eyes are set in a mask of indifference, and his blue eyes are so light they're almost invisible, like grey sand on a beach. He's a tall man, with a lean face, and a chiseled jaw, and he could have been handsome, if not for the cold, indifferent glare.

Kurt comes next, a boy, and the first to notice the escalator's passengers is a little girl, both of them on an adventure. Their parents are in a hurry, and so they've been left in the care of the ride. The boy and girl are orphans, and the escalator is their playground. They take and love the escalator for its movement and sound, and for the way it makes them feel, weightless. The little girl, in a dress, is the image of innocence, and the picture of trouble. She's on her way to mischief, and the boy, on his way to trouble, is with him.

The next to arrive is Maria, a housewife, who's on her way to a party. It's an event for a cause, for the less fortunate. She's not one for social functions, but this one promises to be different. It's not often that you get to learn about the struggles of others in the comfort of an air-conditioned room, with wine, and cheese. She's a little late, and she's a little flustered, but she's not alone. Her husband is with her, a tall man, with a sturdy frame, and a kind face. He's a man of few words, and even fewer friends,
